Escape the Backrooms is more than just another mediocre attempt at making a Backrooms game. It's a well made, rather lore accurate game that is decently scary during half of the game. Not to mention the game looks incredible for being just $10, and it runs well most of the time. All the future updates appear to be free, and each new update makes the experience all the more interesting. I'd give this game a 8/10, since although its only early access, players can expect a well made liminal exploration game, that incorporates elements of horror, infinity, and feelings of familiarity.
It is really scary but yet really interesting it is important to NOT play alone so the person in front of you gets eaten first

This is surprisingly quite good. Grabbed it with friend and expected just few minutes laugh with low effort game but that is not what this is at all. It really surprised in the length and quality. Solid few hours of entertaining horror/fun experience. Gotta say for someone who doesnt like these sneak and puzzles and monster chasing etc, it is bit of anxiety at some points but fun nonetheless. Have nothing bad to say.

This game is easily the most flushed out and detailed Backrooms games currently available on Steam.
I was a bit hesitant to purchase after seeing a lot of mixed refused but I decided to just bite the bullet and do it. Here is my honest opinion and some pros and cons. 

Pros: 
-Multiple levels. (ranging in difficulty significantly, in no particular order.) 
-Fun and pretty terrifying at times.
-Really good graphics.
-Multiplayer mode. (Haven't touched it yet because I have no friends)

Cons:
-A set, laid out path that does not differ between playthrough to playthrough. No randomization like most Backrooms games/lore.
-Some AI/monster bugs, especially in the second to last level. That level is also extremely long and not very fun relative to other levels.
-Some RNG when it comes to beating Level Fun! in a certain section. Beating it seems to depend on spawn locations of some Partygoers. (Maybe I'm just bad.)
-Very small parts of the game incomplete or lacking graphics wise.

Overall, this game is very polished and flushed out. Some bugs make certain sections of this game slightly annoying- but nothing that's impossible to get past. The path isn't plainly laid out so referring to a guide or walkthrough is definitely recommended. Unfortunately, if you do this the game can go by quite quickly. (I completed in just over 2 hours.) And the replayablility isn't quite there unless you're playing multiplayer. 

If you're a fan of the Backrooms, this game is the best currently on the market. It is more than a great time and will give you some good scares. Would definitely recommend.

If you're not a Backrooms fan but this game still looks interesting, I would wait until the game goes on sale or has been a bit more polished.

This backrooms game by far is the most accurate and fun I've had. It's a fun game to play with friends and can amp up your experience. If your looking for a full on backrooms game with all or most the levels in it, well it's getting there but currently has 16 levels which some are popular in the lore. I would definitely be down to help if I could, once I get some free time if needed(Im a 3d environment artist). 

Here are some great things I like about the game:
+Has a variety of levels for early access(16 at the moment)with its own unique puzzles and entities
+The entities in the game are pretty accurate from the backrooms lore
+The places or levels are fairly accurate to the original lore with just level 0 being a bit different
+The game has a variety of difficulties so you can choose what fits your play style best
+There is an inventory system along with items you can use to help you in each level
+Multiplayer is a huge plus and makes the game fun, even with others it can be scary
+I believe this game is made with UE4 or 5 and UE is an amazing engine, especially for artists

Rather than list some cons here are just some suggestions or things I would love to see in time:
-More variety of levels from the lore that are fairly popular and fit in well. I know this one will take time so there is no rush but there are some levels that just make no sense so I would avoid those ones or customize the lore on them.
-More entities from the lore or even custom ones, again will take a lot more time as animation and character modeling is a long process.
-The hub expanded eventually to house more levels to go to.
-Some of the entities can glitch in some areas and i'm sure this is being worked out or will be over time.
- I think it would be nice to expand some of the levels more and maybe have some randomization to them so they don't have the same layout. Possibly have entrances to other levels within that are randomized when or if the game gets more levels. That way the game could either be long or a bit shorter for play through's depending on choices. The levels don't need to be long mazes just a bit more bigger with maybe a bit more to explore.
- Having more variety of items or just options to deal with certain entities that are very rare.

I can't really think of too many suggestions or things to see atm but I feel like the game is going in the right direction. Fancy keep doing what your doing and please continue to work on the game. I always wanted to make a game similar to the backrooms but I never had the time or programming skills to do it since I'm an artist only. If you need help I would be down and I'm sure many others are willing to help. I feel like this game could be amazing and your approach makes it less boring because it isn't just a maze but you can actually get to levels without it being a long journey in just one level. It would be cool to see M.E.G members or something later with missions for us to do if we survive and maybe get rewarded.

Currently a 9/10 for me!

I beat the game and it was a lot of fun to play with friends and with proximity chat. There are some very hard parts but you can look up guides on how to do stuff. I didn't go into this game blind but if I did it would probably be 150% more fun. Go into the game with an open mind it will be an amazing experience with your friends.

Now, when you first install this game, which is an action I highly recommend, your first thought will very possible be, "man this game looks like crap." However, it's not all about that. What its about is the thrill, the fun, and the exhilaration of running on infinite stamina screaming with your friends from some murderous thing. If you can get your friends to get it, please give it a chance, the levels get even more fun as the game progresses and your gang of hazmat fellas gets sillier.

Honestly I don't know why people are complaining. I have beaten this game before solo and in multiplayer while it was still developed only by Fancy and it is still hands down the best backrooms game. Every level, every monster is very unique and you do not get bored while playing at all. I have only scratched the surface of the game in 1.0 and I am already having a ton of fun discovering all the new things in old levels. 

Keep in mind, before Secret Mode publisher joined, Escape the Backrooms was developed by ONE guy, who put all his free time to develop the game, adding new things while also polishing the rest. It's amazing seeing all his progress in only 2 years, while also keeping the price not only very affordable but also the same with what it was initially. The amount of content you get for the price you pay is way more than fair and I very much recommend it to both solo gamers and to play with friends. You won't regret it

After playing Escape the Backrooms, I can confidently say that I 100% recommend this game. Even after completing it, I found myself wishing there was more to play because I genuinely enjoyed every moment of the experience.

This game delivered exactly what I was hoping for and created so many great memories with my friends. There were plenty of genuinely scary moments that made me jump out of my seat or scream down the microphone, but what I valued most was how it brought happiness, teamwork, and, most importantly, laughter to our group.

There were countless moments where we laughed so hard we could barely breathe due to how we died throughout the different levels. For the best experience possible, I highly recommend playing with friends. While playing solo can certainly be tense and immersive, experiencing the game as a group creates unforgettable memories that make it even more enjoyable.

Throughout my playthrough, I ended up collecting loads of funny clips and even where we were scared. The developers did an incredible job designing each level, the escape mechanics, and the various entities you encounter along the way. Every level felt unique and engaging.

The proximity chat system also deserves special praise, as it adds so much to the atmosphere and overall enjoyment. It’s clear that this game was designed with cooperative play in mind, so I'd suggest to not play it alone.

Beyond the gameplay itself, the game sparked my interest in the wider Backrooms lore. It encouraged me to dive deeper into the concept, explore its stories, and even made me watch the movie that came out and it certainly didn't fail to deliver. It genuinely showed how unique the backrooms truly is and how much of a terrifying place it can be.

On top of all that, the price is excellent considering the amount of content available. With so many levels to explore and experiences to discover, it offers incredible value for money and most importantly funny moments with your friends.

Overall, Escape the Backrooms is one of the most memorable games I've ever played and I would highly recommend it to anyone looking for scares, laughs, and unforgettable moments with friends. Since there is a variety of levels, the game can last you a long time depending how much time you spend on it.

[b]INGREDIENTS[/b]
- 500ml of mineral water

Place the almonds in the mixing bowl, pour in tap water, and let the bowl sit for an hour. When that hour is up, dump out the water using the strainer.

[b]STEP 2[/b]
Using the food processor, lightly pulse the almonds until they’re coarsely chopped.

[b]STEP 3[/b]
Now that the almonds are ground, place them, along with the 500 millilitres of mineral water and 100 grams of the cane sugar, into the cooking pot, and bring it to a boil. It is the first part of making the “syrup” that’ll accompany the water.

[b]STEP 4[/b]
When boiled, turn off the heat. Now, you have two options here: you can either leave the mixture in the pot and cover it or pour it into a container of your choosing. No matter which option you choose, you have to let the mixture sit for 12 hours.

[b]STEP 5[/b]
After the 12 hours have gone by, strain the mixture through the cheesecloth, and place the liquid in the mixing bowl and add the cane sugar. I should also note that the sugar should be 1.4 times the quantity of the liquid. It helps when you dilute the water.

[b]STEP 6[/b]
Once the sugar is poured in, pour the mixture back into the cooking pot. It’s important to note that you want to place the cooking pot on low heat. If you bring the pot to a boil, it will burn the sugar. With that being said, stir the sugar until it’s dissolved.

[b]STEP 7[/b]
Now that the sugar is dissolved, turn off the heat and let the mixture cool down. Once cooled, add a few drops of the almond and vanilla extracts.

[b]STEP 8[/b]
Once you’ve poured the extracts, grab the container you’ll be using to store the almond water. If you want assurance that the bottle is clean, you can boil some water and pour the boiling water into it. Make sure you pour in the water with caution if you decide to do this. Once this is done, empty the bottle out.

[b]STEP 9[/b]
Now that we’ve emptied the bottle of the boiling (if you chose to do that), pour in the almond mixture you just heated in the pot. And once the mixture is poured into the bottle, let the bottle sit until it’s cool enough to handle, and then refrigerate.

[b]STEP 10[/b]
Once its ready to use, dilute the syrup in water to taste. Fucking delicious, but don't forget to shake well before drinking. Enjoy!

[h2]I have mixed feelings[/h2]

First off, i want to say that i [u]played this solo[/u]. It feels like it was intended to be played with others so my opinion might be different in that aspect.
Now that i have finally beaten the game i want to leave a review. I have to say, they nailed the backrooms vibes perfectly (in some levels at least). Levels  such as lvl 3999, lvl 4, lvl 10, just to name a few really had that liminal vibe to them. The puzzles also weren't too bad. But there is one big thing that really brought down my enjoyment with this game - the [u]monsters[/u].
[u]Monsters[/u] were the worst part of thing game. In rare cases like lvl 10 the monster was a nice addition that scared you from time to time but wasn't really a problem. But in 80% of the levels with monsters, those were so annoying i just couldn't force myself to play more than a few (3-4) levels in one sitting if all of them had monsters. Monsters very often just sat near the entrance to the level, or next to the objective and often wouldn't move at all from there, so i had to lure them out by showing myself and getting killed. And stuff like this was pretty common. Other thing is that sometimes (mostly in the earlier levels) after successfully hiding myself the entity just wouldn't go away. Maybe it wouldn't happen that often if i were playing with others so other players would aggro the monsters but oh well.
My another main [u]problem[/u] were some of the levels like lvl 5 - it's 3rd part to be exact. It was a labirynth, which is to be expected from backrooms game. But it was filled with entities, and to leave you had to walk next to them. But guess what? The game doesn't tell you that you can just crouch near them and they will 100% ignore you, no matter how close to them you are. They even do the opposite by giving you an item that show where the entity is sitting so you won't get close. If i didn't just google the answer i'd probably be stuck there forever.
I want to recommend this game, but it really makes me have mixed feeling. On one hand you have well done levels, most of them really unique, well reflecting the levels they are based on, but on the other hand you have really annoying and sometimes just tedious gameplay, all because of the entities. The game is pretty cheap tho, so it's not like you lose much if you don't like the game. I will keep the review as positive, but remember that it's mostly a mixed for me.

I want to be careful with what I say because I am a hobbyist game developer myself and know the time and effort that is put into things like this. But to be as frank as possible, the game just isn't good. 

Visually the game is fantastic, it is perhaps the most "accurate" portrayal of the backrooms I have seen in any game, and looks stunning without killing my frame rate issues.

Gameplay-wise, it is a game I wouldn't recommend anyone buy for $9.99. In short, the game simply lacks good game design. A couple of examples would be the ending of the party room, in which the player is meant to hide under the table to make their way across the room full of enemies. You are able to barely make it if you time everything properly. The result of you failing is getting to slowly make your way through the level again. This is one of the examples I see as the dev equating hard for no reason with "challenging," and challenging inherently being worth the effort. 

The End is a level that made me go on my own philosophical journey about game design as I died again and again to the monster. This level simply lacks any kind of gimmick or really any kind of gameplay mechanic at all. Playing with friends, we tried many different things from moving slowly, running fast, standing still if it saw us, etc. The fact of the matter is, this is just a monster that roams, and if it sees you, you die. No place to hide, no way to outrun it, if it sees you, you die. And if there is a gameplay mechanic, it just does not work,

I think the issue with a lot of indie game devs is that in their minds, making the game hard = making the game fun. But there is no satisfaction in beating a hard level if it makes you think you should have beaten it 20 attempts ago. When done well, a challenging game makes the player think the inability to win is a flaw of their own they need to overcome. In this game, I can't help but see it as a flaw in the game.

You should buy this game if you are up for a horror game with Backrooms stuff in it. The environment does a very good job at making you think you are in the Backrooms and figuring stuff out with friends can be fun.

Do note that I said "horror game with Backrooms stuff in it" and not "Backrooms game with horror stuff in it". Important distinction. If you came here for a Backrooms game, you will be heavily disappointed. The creator missed what made the Backrooms charming in the first place and instead made a generic, linear horror game where you avoid monsters at every corner with nothing but the ability to run (and sometimes, to hide).

The Backrooms are interesting because of [b] uncertainty [/b].
Here, once you've played through the game once or even watched somebody else play it, you've learned all there is to know about the game. The order you play the levels in are not random, but always the same. The terrain layout is not randomly and procedurally generated, but always the same. The entities you encounter are not random per level, but always the same. You will never feel truly desperate for being lost or stuck somewhere because you will always have YouTube guides to help you out, since the content is [i] always the same [/i].

The Backrooms are interesting because of [b] exploration [/b].
Here, exploration is disincentivised. Way too many levels have lethal entities for the sake of having them and not for the sake of serving an actual purpose. The horror of the Backrooms comes from not knowing if there is danger lurking or not. Here, you just open your inventory to check if your sanity drains, and if it does, you will play the level slightly more carefully. You won't think to yourself "I wonder what entities could be in here?". You will think to yourself "Ugh, another headache to avoid." after already experiencing 10 other prior headaches.

Though, even ignoring the Backrooms as a theme, this game doesn't even stand up as its own thing due to poor balancing and design choices. And these choices are not infrequent, much less hard to come by.

The entities themselves are nothing to write home about. After playing like 5 levels, you will quickly realise you either need to run from an entity, crouch around it, or enter a certain area to stay safe. And if none work, you just turn on a valve or hide under a bed or in a closet. Few of the levels innovate (almost as if most entities in the game are redundant, as mentioned above). The entity balancing is all over the place. Some of them exist around corners in dead ends for cheap deaths and jumpscares like in level electrical station or level fun; some of them have horrible AI that cannot be predicted and does whatever it wants like the entity in level the end; sometimes it's the level's fault for being half-assed, like the mimic section of the level cave, where the cave is not so cave-y and instead is just two very long corridors, making the mimics nigh-impossible to avoid because there is simply nowhere to hide from their sight. Last but not least, there's not enough sound cues to alert you of a nearby entity's presence. Some of them make footstep sounds, but not all of them (out of the ones that have legs, anyway). Mimics and clumps, especially, are in dire need of them because they always appear in levels with sharp turns, have unpredictable movement and once they see you, they never lose track of you.

Two other big culprits that ruin the game are the sanity system and inventory loss upon death. The mere existence of these systems makes you lose braincells because of how godawful they are. Not only do they not improve the game AT ALL in ANY WAY WHATSOEVER, they even contradict eachother's purpose. Sanity system forces you to speedrun the game (since item supply is simply not enough to sustain a full team in some of the levels) and not dilly-dally, whereas the inventory loss forces you to play it safely and slowly. Sanity promotes stocking up on items while inventory loss wants you not to grow reliant on your items. Which one is it‽‽‽ Absolutely zero braincells were used in the addition of these mechanics.

Then there's the items, specifically the food consumables. Like I said, the sanity system is trash, so almond water is just a bandage for that trash. The energy bars are just worse almond waters since you can't see your stamina and everybody bunny-hops anyway. Moth jelly is too rare to be worth talking about. The only consumable that has consistent value is the juice. Though even the juice is made bad by the fact that the speed boost lasts about as much as it takes you to drink it. After you drink juice, by the time you open inventory, place new juice from inventory to your hotbar and close inventory, half of the effect is already gone.

Then there are levels that had potential to be fun, but the developer didn't quite understand their purpose, like the level lights out ( and of course, this level also has a useless entity.... because this game totally does not have enough entities!!!11!1!) or level thalassophobia, so they ended up just being there, like placeholders.

For the trophy hunters among us, something that should be addressed is the fact that beating the game on a higher difficulty does not automatically also grant you the achievements for the difficulties below it.

A final, very important question: Where Steam Workshop?

Escape the Backrooms: The Definitive Backrooms Experience on Steam
Having explored every corner of this game and even conquered its toughest challenge—the Nightmare achievement—I can confidently say that Escape the Backrooms is the best Backrooms game you can find on Steam. It’s a genuinely terrifying experience that’s absolutely worth your time.

The game is a masterclass in atmospheric horror. Its entities are genuinely frightening, and the sheer terror of hearing a sound down a hallway when you're playing alone is bone-chilling. The game's value comes from its sheer amount of content, featuring dozens of levels to explore, each with its own unique design and challenges. The developers have also promised to add a new map every month, which ensures there's always something new to fear. While the solo experience is terrifying, the game is also incredibly fun in multiplayer, where the tension is often broken by moments of pure, unscripted chaos and laughter.

Pros
Terrifyingly Effective Entities: The monsters and atmosphere do an excellent job of creating genuine fear, especially when you're playing alone.

Vast Amount of Content: With dozens of levels and more promised on the way, the game offers a ton of gameplay for the price.

Endless Multiplayer Fun: Playing with friends adds a hilarious and chaotic layer to the terrifying survival experience.

Cons
Puzzles Lack Depth: The puzzles are generally quite easy and simple, especially when compared to a game like Inside the Backrooms.

Limited Communication Options: The game could benefit from an option to switch between proximity chat and open chat, which would improve communication and strategy.

Small Player Base: The online community can be sparse, so finding a match with randoms can be difficult.

Occasional Bugs: While most bugs are minor, some can be game-breaking, like getting randomly thrown into a different level.

Final Score
9/10

Escape the Backrooms is a must-play for fans of the genre. It delivers a solid, terrifying, and content-rich experience that stands out from the competition.
